newsitem.title: USA: US spot distillates fall on NYMEX, weaker diffs.
newsitem.headline: US spot distillates fall on NYMEX, weaker diffs.

text.p: U.S. spot distillate prices fell sharply late Thursday tracking NYMEX futures, players said, with differentials easing in both centers amid volatility throughout the day.

Gulf Coast differentials were "every bit as volatile as the Merc (NYMEX)," one distillate trader said, with low sulfur diesel weakening about 1.50 cents a gallon in the morning to about 2.50 cents over March futures.
By late afternoon, however, USG low sulfur bounced back to about 3.80 cents over the print despite reports some refinery units had been returned to service following maintenance turnarounds.
Star Enterprise said it would restart Friday a 35,000 barrel per day heavy oil unit at its Convent, Louisiana, refinery.

The unit was shut Dec 4 after a fire, helping support distillate prices in recent weeks -- particularly low sulphur diesel -- as Star and other refiners bid for scarce barrels in the Gulf Coast, traders said.
New York Harbor low sulfur diffs slipped about 0.40 cent to 3.0 cents over the print.
